[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roundtable intro — I'm Samir, AE on the partnerships team at Redwood. Leah is our systems engineer and will do the tech bits, Maya runs partner programs.

[00:58] Priya (Aurora): Quick question, what does private deployment look like from a networking perspective? We typically offer VPC peering and also customer managed on‑prem installs.
[01:12] Leah (Redwood): We support VPC peering and direct connect. For on‑prem we have a private deployment package — control plane can be customer managed, and we integrate with KMS/HSM for key management. There's some ops work up front but it's designed for regulated workloads.
[01:35] Liam (Aurora): And latency? A lot of our customers care about sub‑50ms token latency for chat workloads. How do you guarantee that?
[01:48] Leah (Redwood): We have a serving runtime optimized for GPUs, continuous batching, KV cache for prefixes, and kernel selection. For sub‑50ms at scale it's typically a combination of dedicated capacity + model variant tuning. We can benchmark with your workloads — different models and sequence lengths change the profile a lot.
[02:10] Samir (Redwood): From a partner angle, we're interested in Aurora as a channel partner to offer Dedicated/Private deployments bundled with your infra. Also curious about reseller economics — revenue share, referral fees, etc. Maya will follow up on program specifics.
[02:28] Ethan (Aurora): Sounds good. A couple business constraints: many of our enterprise clients require SOC2, SSO (SAML/Okta), and audit logs. They also ask for data residency. Do you have those covered?
[02:44] Maya (Redwood): Yes — we have SOC2, ISO in flight, SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC, and detailed audit logs. For data residency we can run private deployments in region or support region‑specific Dedicated pools. We'll share the compliance pack.
[03:05] Priya (Aurora): For the integration itself, we're thinking two flavors: 1) reseller where we provide the infra + support and Redwood provides the control plane and model stack; or 2) deeper integration where we embed Redwood SDK into our portal and offer one‑click deployments. Both have pros/cons on ops and revenue.
[03:29] Samir (Redwood): Both are viable. Reseller is faster to market; embedded is better for long term stickiness. We usually recommend starting with a pilot/reseller offering then building an integration if it proves out.
[03:45] Liam (Aurora): From the technical checklist — does Redwood support custom model deployment (customers bring their own models), or only curated model catalog?
[03:58] Leah (Redwood): We support both. Hosted has curated models; Dedicated/Private can run customer models. We support common formats and provide quantization guidance. For BYO models we usually run a quick onboarding to validate kernel support and perf.
[04:20] Ethan (Aurora): Perf tests are key. Can we run a benchmark against a T4 and an H100 cluster we have? We'll want a cost/latency matrix.
[04:32] Leah (Redwood): Absolutely. We'll define a test corpus and latency targets. Leah: action — get me sample prompts and expected concurrency. We'll spin up comparable model variants and report tokens/sec, p95 latency, and cost per token.
[04:50] Priya (Aurora): A note on security: some clients require KMS + HSM integration — do you support customer‑owned KMS?
[04:59] Leah (Redwood): Yes customer KMS is supported; we can integrate with AWS KMS and external HSMs for key wraps.
[05:10] Ethan (Aurora): What about billing/committing? If we resell Dedicated pools do we need a minimum commit?
[05:20] Samir (Redwood): Dedicated is typically reserved with monthly/annual commits. We can create partner pricing tiers. We'll share examples in the partner program deck.
[05:35] Maya (Redwood): Also for partner enablement we have co‑sell materials, playbooks, and a partner portal. We can provide enablement sessions for your sales and solutions teams.
[05:48] Liam (Aurora): Are there existing partners doing similar integrations? Curious about references.
[05:55] Samir (Redwood): We've worked with a few cloud partners and GPU vendors; we can share anonymized reference notes.
[06:05] Ethan (Aurora): On the integration APIs — does Redwood expose a stable REST/SDK with streaming and function calling?
[06:13] Leah (Redwood): Yes. REST + official SDKs, streaming responses, function/tool calling. Also embeddings and reranking endpoints.
[06:25] Priya (Aurora): Any constraints on model sizes for private deployments? Some of our infra has memory limits.
[06:33] Leah (Redwood): We recommend quantization profiles for larger models. We also support sharded KV cache and have kernel selection per architecture. We'll work with your infra team.
[06:50] Samir (Redwood): Let's talk partner commercial structure — we typically do referral fees for simple referrals and revenue share for co‑sold accounts. Maya will outline program tiers.
[07:02] Maya (Redwood): Program tiers: Referral, Reseller (white‑label), Strategic (joint go‑to‑market with co‑sell). Each has different SLAs and enablement commitments. We'll send the tier doc.
[07:18] Ethan (Aurora): Good. For pilots — we prefer a 6‑8 week pilot with two customer profiles and a benchmark report at the end. Is that workable?
[07:27] Samir (Redwood): Yes. Typical pilot includes setup, benchmark runs, and a short eval period. We can attach success criteria: latency p95, cost per 1k tokens, and error rate.
[07:42] Leah (Redwood): Technical deep dive items to cover in follow up: network topology, VPC peering, KMS flow, model upload process, quantization options, autoscaling policies, and fallback routing.
[08:00] Liam (Aurora): For autoscaling — do you allow burst capacity? On our side, workloads can spike 10x.
[08:09] Leah (Redwood): Yes, dedicated pools can be configured with burst capacity. There's a policy that balances cost vs guaranteed throughput.
[08:20] Ethan (Aurora): A couple of client asks: audit logs retention 1 year minimum, SSO, and per‑token billing breakdown — are all available?
[08:30] Maya (Redwood): Yes audit logs retention configurable (add‑on for longer), SSO via SAML/OIDC. Token‑level cost breakdown is in our console and we can expose APIs for usage.
[08:45] Samir (Redwood): Any blockers from Aurora on logos, legal or procurement before we send partner materials?
[08:52] Priya (Aurora): We'll need to see data processing terms and reseller agreement. Procurement sits on those. Also client references are helpful.
[09:02] Maya (Redwood): We'll include DPA and reseller terms in the follow up package.
[09:10] Ethan (Aurora): Tech question — if a customer wants their own model, will Redwood handle fine‑tuning or do we need to do that on our infra?
[09:22] Leah (Redwood): We don't provide training in hosted mode; fine‑tuning can be done upstream and then deployed to Dedicated/Private. We can help with inference optimizations post‑tuning.
[09:35] Liam (Aurora): Regarding model variants — how do rollouts work? Canary, A/B?
[09:42] Leah (Redwood): We support canary rollouts, A/B testing, and automatic fallback to compatible variants if capacity is constrained.
[09:55] Samir (Redwood): Great — let's outline the pilot plan and responsibilities.
[10:00] Priya (Aurora): We'll be responsible for infra and initial customer introductions; you'll be responsible for control plane and model infra.
